In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lin-4-mediated repression of lin-14 protein is due to both translational and post-transcriptional mRNA degradation mechanisms.
lin-14 mRNA is destabilized by lin-4, and that lin-4-mediated translational inhibition is required to achieve the full silencing of LIN-14 expression.

lin-4 miRNAs regulate lin-14 mRNA in two distinct ways: (i) lin-4 miRNP complexes bind to multiple sites in the lin4 3′UTRs, and the resulting inhibition of translation of the lin4 mRNA is dependent on these multiple binding sites, and (ii) lin-4 binding to a single target site in the lin4 mRNA causes the degradation of the mRNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lin-4 miRNAs bind with partial complementarily to the lin-14 target mRNA to inhibit translation and destabilize the mRNA, but the translational inhibition is more significant.
the lin-4 microRNA (miRNA) is an important regulator of the lin-1 4 mRNA, but that the lin-1 mRNA is not a simple target of the lin- 4 miRNA.
the lin-4 mRNA has a complex regulatory role in the control of lin-14.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lin-4 microRNA is a potent regulator of lin-14 protein levels.
the lin-4-mediated repression of lin-14 protein levels involves a dual mechanism of translational inhibition and mRNA destabilization.
translational inhibition is an important mechanism for miRNA-mediated gene silencing, and that miRNA-mediated translational repression can be achieved by multiple binding sites in the 3’UTR.
